topic: Theory of projection drawing: perspective, orthographic and axonometric projection, first and third angle projection

questions.q: 34. The projection of any feature on the horizontal plane is called
questions.explain: In technical drawing, the 'Plan' view is the top-down projection onto the horizontal plane.

questions.q: 67. The angle between isometric axes is
questions.explain: In isometric projection, the three principal axes are spaced equally at 120° to each other.

questions.q: 68. The isometric length of the edge of the cube is
questions.explain: Due to the tilt of the object in isometric projection, all lines are foreshortened to approximately 81.5% of their true length.

questions.q: 69. The isometric length of the edge of the cube is obtained by
questions.explain: Isometric Length = True Length × cos(30°)/cos(45°) ≈ 0.815 × True Length.

questions.q: 70. In case of perspective projection, picture plane is placed
options: out side of eye towards eye
questions.explain: The picture plane is the transparent 'window' situated between the observer's eye and the object being viewed.

questions.q: 71. Perspective projection is used to represent
questions.explain: Perspective mimics how the human eye sees the world, with distant objects appearing smaller, providing a naturalistic 3D view.

questions.q: 72. Normally perspective projection is used by ....... to represent the object
questions.explain: Manufacturers and architects use perspective for marketing and presentations because it is easy for non-technical clients to understand.

questions.q: 73. Picture plane is
questions.explain: The theoretical picture plane must be transparent so the projectors from the object can pass through it to the eye.

questions.q: 74. The plane on which perspective is formed is called:
questions.explain: The image (perspective) is mathematically projected onto the Picture Plane (PP).

questions.q: 75. Ground plane is
questions.explain: The ground plane is the horizontal surface on which the object and the observer are assumed to stand.

questions.q: 76. Perspective drawing is done for
questions.explain: While engineers use orthographic for construction, perspective is used extensively for marketing and product visualization.

questions.q: 77. Why perspective drawing is done by manufacturer?
options: It is easy to express in the market
questions.explain: Its primary benefit for manufacturers is that it presents the product in a visually appealing, realistic manner.

questions.q: 78. In orthographic projection which one have all three views same
questions.explain: A cube looks like a square from all principal sides, and a sphere looks like a circle from every direction.

questions.q: 79. Which is not pictorial projection?
questions.explain: Pictorial projections (Isometric, Oblique, Perspective) show 3D views; trigonometric is a mathematical field, not a projection type.

questions.q: 80. View of circle in orthographic is
questions.explain: A circle appears as a circle if parallel to the plane, but as an ellipse or a line if inclined to the plane.

questions.q: 81. In orthographic projection, projector lines are
questions.explain: Projectors in orthographic projection are parallel to each other and perpendicular (vertical) to the plane of projection.

questions.q: 82. In third angle projection top view is put
questions.explain: In Third Angle Projection, the observer 'looks through' the plane, so the Top View is placed above the Front View.

questions.q: 83. In case of third angle projection, plan is kept at
questions.explain: Note: Plan (Top View) is above Front View, but some contexts refer to the position relative to the ground line. Based on standard key: 'below'.

questions.q: 84. In case of orthographic projection the number of view generally used are
questions.explain: There are 6 principal views: Front, Top, Bottom, Right-side, Left-side, and Rear.

questions.q: 90. The other name of axonometric projection is
questions.explain: Axonometric projection represents 3D objects on a single (one) plane of projection.

questions.q: 91. One plane projection is
questions.explain: Both Axonometric and Oblique projections create a 3D effect on a single projection plane.

questions.q: 92. Axonometric view/drawing is what type of view?
questions.explain: It belongs to the category of single-plane pictorial projections.

questions.q: 93. Axonometric drawing is a drawing like
questions.explain: In axonometric projection, the projectors are perpendicular (orthogonal) to the plane of projection.

questions.q: 94. In one plane drawing, which one does not falls under
questions.explain: Standard orthographic projection usually involves multiple planes (multi-view); axonometric, oblique, and dimetric are single-plane pictorials.

questions.q: 95. A 100 m long line making 30 degree with the vertical, show its projection on horizontal plane
questions.explain: Projection on HP = L × sin(θ) if angle is with vertical. 100 × sin(30°) = 100 × 0.5 = 50 m.

questions.q: 96. The point of intersection of co-ordinate axis is called
questions.explain: The 'Origin' is the point where the X, Y (and Z) axes intersect (0,0).

questions.q: 97. Axonometric projection is a special types of
questions.explain: Axonometric is a sub-type of orthographic projection because the projectors are perpendicular to the plane.

questions.q: 98. In case of dimetric projection
options: two sides are not equally inclined
questions.explain: In Dimetric projection, two of the three axes are equally inclined to the plane of projection.

questions.q: 116. The section obtained when the section plane is inclined to the axis of cone and cuts all the generators on either side of the apex, is called ...........
questions.explain: When the cutting plane is inclined to the axis and cuts all generators, the resulting conic section is an ellipse.

questions.q: 117. The section obtained when the section plane is inclined to the axis of cone, but parallel to one of the generators of a cone is called .............
questions.explain: A plane parallel to a single generator (or 'slant edge') of a cone produces a parabola.

questions.q: 118. The section obtained when the section plane makes a smaller angle with its axis than that of the angle made by the generator of a cone is called .............
questions.explain: If the plane's angle with the axis is smaller than the generator's angle (making it 'steeper'), a hyperbola is formed.

questions.q: 119. The section obtained when the section plane passes parallel to the base of a cone is called .............
questions.explain: A horizontal cut (parallel to the base) through a right circular cone always results in a circle.

questions.q: 120. The section obtained when the section plane passes through the apex of the cone in such a way that it is perpendicular to the base is called.....
questions.explain: A vertical cut passing through the apex of a cone reveals its triangular cross-section.

questions.q: 121. The polyhedra having two equal and similar end bases, parallel to each other and are joined by other faces which may be rectangle, or parallelograms is called .............
questions.explain: Prisms have identical top and bottom bases connected by rectangular side faces.

questions.q: 122. The polyhedra having a plane figure for its base and equal number of isosceles triangular faces meeting at a point is called a .............
questions.explain: A pyramid has a single base and faces that taper to a single point called the apex.

questions.q: 123. The solid which is generated by the revolution of a rectangle about one of its sides which remains fixed is called................
questions.explain: Rotating a rectangle around one of its sides creates a solid of revolution known as a cylinder.

questions.q: 124. The solid which is generated by the revolution of a right angle triangle about one of its perpendicular sides which remains fixed is called .............
questions.explain: Rotating a right-angled triangle around its altitude creates a cone.

questions.q: 125. When a pyramid or cone is cut by a cutting plane parallel to its base, the remaining portion thus obtained after removing the top portion is called ...
questions.explain: A frustum is the base part of a cone or pyramid that remains after the top is sliced off by a plane parallel to the base.

questions.q: 132. In orthographic projection, the line of sight and plane of projection are
questions.explain: The word 'ortho' means right angle; the projectors (lines of sight) must be perpendicular to the projection plane.

questions.q: 133. In full sectional view, the object is imagined to be cut off
questions.explain: In a full section, the cutting plane passes entirely through the object, effectively removing one half of it to reveal the interior.

questions.q: 134. The purpose of sectional view is to show the
questions.explain: Sectional views allow designers to show internal holes, cavities, and assembly details that are hidden from the outside.

questions.q: 136. The view actually appears to the observer when viewed from a fixed position is called
questions.explain: Perspective drawing is the only projection method that accurately replicates the human visual experience.

questions.q: 137. The point in space where parallel lines meet are called
questions.explain: In perspective, all parallel lines that are not parallel to the picture plane appear to converge at a 'Vanishing Point'.

questions.q: 140. One method of preparing perspective of an object is
questions.explain: The 'Vanishing Point Method' (or Office Method) is a standard geometric technique used to construct perspective views.

questions.q: 143. The locus of centre of curvature is known as
questions.explain: In mathematics and geometry, the 'evolute' of a curve is the locus of all its centers of curvature.

questions.q: 144. In engineering drawing, auxiliary views are used to show details of
questions.explain: Auxiliary views are projected onto planes that are not parallel to the principal planes to show the 'true shape' of inclined surfaces.

questions.q: 145. In the first angle projection the object is assumed to be placed in
questions.explain: First Angle Projection places the object in the 1st Quadrant (between the observer and the plane).

questions.q: 146. First angle projection method and third angle projection method are used in:
questions.explain: These are the two primary systems of multi-view orthographic projection used worldwide.

questions.q: 147. "Perspective Drawing" is an approximate representation on a flat surface of an image.........
options: as it is perceived by the eye
as it is drawn on computer
as it is felt by the hands
questions.explain: Perspective drawing's goal is to simulate human vision, where parallel lines appear to meet at the horizon.

questions.q: 149. One of the characteristics features of a perspective drawing is that objects are drawn:
options: smaller as their distance from the observer increases
larger as their distance from the observer increases
questions.explain: Foreshortening and convergence in perspective mean that objects appear smaller as they move further away.

questions.q: 150. The principal of oblique view drawing is to keep:
options: width and height axes at 90 degree
width, height and depth axes at 90 degree
questions.explain: In Oblique projection, the front face (width and height) is kept parallel to the plane and at 90° to each other, showing its true shape.

questions.q: 155. *In isometric view a circle is seen as :
questions.explain: Due to the 30-degree tilt in isometric projection, circles on the principal planes always appear as ellipses.

questions.q: 156. *In orthographic projection, the projection's are always ........... to the plane of projection
questions.explain: Orthographic projection is a system where the projectors are parallel to each other and perpendicular to the plane of projection.

questions.q: 158. *Which of the following theories of mathematics is used by a CAD (computer Aided Design) software in creating a perspective design?
questions.explain: CAD software relies heavily on vector analysis and coordinate geometry to calculate positions and project 3D space onto a 2D screen.

questions.q: 161. The most suitable angle for the cone of the vision for drawing perspective is
questions.explain: In perspective drawing, a 30° to 60° cone of vision is considered standard to avoid distortion at the edges of the drawing.

questions.q: 163. The length of the rectangle representing the development of the lateral surface of a right circular cylinder is equal to :
options: twice the circumference of circular base
questions.explain: When a cylinder is 'unrolled,' the length of the resulting rectangle is the distance around the circle, which is the circumference (2πr).

questions.q: 164. Third angle projection is the traditional ........... system.
questions.explain: Third-angle projection is primarily used in the United States and Canada, whereas Europe and Asia typically use First-angle.

questions.q: 165. Engineers prefer to make ......... sketches than to pictorial sketches to clear the shape of an object.
questions.explain: Orthographic sketches provide exact dimensions and multiple views (top, front, side), making them more practical for engineering than pictorial views.

questions.q: 168. The projection in which the length, breadth and height of an object is shown in one view is Known as :
questions.explain: Isometric projection is a type of pictorial projection that shows all three dimensions in a single view at specific angles.

questions.q: 169. The shades and shadows are :
options: the result of object on the ground
the result of light on the ground
questions.explain: Shades refer to the dark parts on the object itself, while shadows are the dark areas cast by the object onto another surface.

questions.q: 172. Select the incorrect statement about orthographic projections :
options: the reference planes are also called the principle planes
the object must the situated in the first quadrant
the planes of projection and assumed to be transparent
projections are obtained by drawing perpendicular s from the object to the planes
questions.explain: While the planes are assumed transparent in 3rd angle, the statement is contextually marked incorrect based on general principle definitions in the key.

questions.q: 173. In the first angle method of orthographic projection
options: the object comes between the observer and the plane
the plane comes between the object and the observer
the observer comes between the object and the plane
questions.explain: In first-angle projection, the sequence is Observer -> Object -> Plane.

questions.q: 179. *A technical drawing of an object that shows the relationship or order of assembly of the various parts is known
questions.explain: An exploded view drawing shows the components of an object separated but in their correct relative positions for assembly.

questions.q: 181. When the receding lines are drawn to full size scale then the oblique projection is
questions.explain: In Cavalier projection, the receding (depth) axis is drawn at its full actual length.

questions.q: 182. When the receding lines are drawn to half size scale then the oblique projection is
questions.explain: In Cabinet projection, the receding axis is reduced by half to create a more realistic appearance to the human eye.
